entries.english:
Niklas der Glosel and his associates sell the monastery their rights to two thirds of the farm at Weidern for 37 pounds of Viennese pennies.

I, Niklas der Glosel von Weydorn, and I, Chünigünd, his wife; I, Peter, and I, Niklas, his sons; I, Kathrei, I, Margaretha, and I, Elisabeth, his daughters; I, Konrad der Ofnêr, his brother; and I, Konrad der Syedenraüttêr, a citizen of St. Pölten; and all our heirs, declare openly by this letter to all who see, hear or read it, living now or in the future, that with careful deliberation, acting jointly and on the advice of our closest and best friends, at a time when we could lawfully do so, we have justly and honestly sold all the rights we had in the two parts of the burgrecht of the farm situated at Weydorn, the remaining third of that farm being held by the noble lady von Rosenberg, sister of Herr Rudolf von Waltse. For the two thirds of the farm held by burgrecht we have also paid annually as burgrecht dues to the reverend spiritual lords, the provost and convent of St. Pölten, forty Metzen of grain, forty Metzen of oats, eight cheeses each worth fifteen Viennese pennies, forty eggs, one goose or eight pennies, and four autumn hens each worth two pennies.

We have sold and given the aforesaid two parts of the burgrecht of the same farm at Weydorn, all the rights we had in them, and everything belonging to them in field and village, whether let or unlet, versücht or unversücht, with all their appurtenant benefits and rights, just as we have held and enjoyed them up to the present day, to our aforesaid gracious lords, Herr Leutold, the provost, and the convent of St. Pölten, to that religious house and all their successors there, for thirty-seven pounds of Viennese pennies. We have received payment in full from them and have paid the money to Jews and other creditors because of great need. Henceforth they shall be free to dispose of our aforesaid two thirds of the burgrecht of the farm, with the rights described above, entirely for their own benefit, selling, pledging or giving them to whomever they wish, without dispute or hindrance.

We are their lawful warrantors and defenders against all claims, as is the law of burgrecht and the law of the land in Austria. If they suffer any lawful loss in this matter, or if any lawful dispute or claim is brought against them by anyone, we shall make all of it good to them and fully compensate them. They may recover this from us without distinction and from all the property we have or may yet acquire in the land of Austria or wherever we hold it, whether we are alive or dead.

In true witness and confirmation we give them this letter sealed with the seals of the honorable lords Herr Heinrich, at that time dean and parish priest at Tüllen, and Herr Michael der Ütendorffer, the official at St. Pölten, and also with the seal of Leb, the judge at St. Pölten. We have earnestly requested them to do this without liability to themselves or to the aforesaid noble lady von Rosenberg, since we ourselves had no seals of our own. Therefore we pledge our fidelity under those seals to hold firmly and carry out everything written above in this letter.

Given on St. Matthias's day before Shrovetide, in the thirteen hundred and seventy-eighth year after Christ's birth.

Seals: of the three seals, only the third remains attached.
